Miracast · device check
A separate diagnostic experiment. This build checks the TV’s actual Android capabilities and can open its system Cast page. It does not yet receive or advertise a Miracast video stream.

Android %1$s has no public WFD configuration API (requires Android 14+). Check the system receiver separately.
Public WFD configuration is listed for this Android version, but this app does not have CONFIGURE_WIFI_DISPLAY. See the device’s permission protection level below.
WFD API and permission are present. This is a prerequisite only; Miracast negotiation, streaming and playback still need implementation.
Wi-Fi Direct feature is reported, but the framework service is unavailable to this app.
Allow a read-only Wi-Fi Direct check?
Android asks for Nearby devices access to read the current Wi-Fi Direct connection and device information. This check does not connect, advertise, or start a scan.

This Android version requires location permission to read Wi-Fi Direct information. Android 12 may also ask for precise location. This app does not read geographic coordinates, scan peers or upload data.
Continue

Permission was not granted. No connection or device-information request was made. You can still inspect the basic report and system settings.

The system Cast page may be for sending to another display. Opening it does not prove the TV can receive Miracast. If the TV has a built-in Wireless display, Screen mirroring, or Multi Visual app, open its receiving mode with the remote.
